text:
RECOMMENDATION: IT DEPENDS
LIKELIHOOD: 35

An all-male panel is not evidence of discrimination by itself — it's context. On its own it proves nothing; plenty of all-male panels appoint women. But combined with other facts it becomes relevant: you had nearly double the relevant experience and five years in the deputy role, and the stated advantage ("strong experience of digital media") is vague and easily used to rationalise a preference after the fact.

The strongest point right now is the silence. Chase the written explanation in writing, with a deadline, and ask specifically how the criteria were scored against each shortlisted candidate. Panel composition is worth mentioning as background — not as your main argument. Let the reasons, or their absence, tell you more.
